ready2_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Consider a linear, time-invariant system whose unit-sample response h[n] is shown in the image. Is it possible to represent this system with a finite number of poles?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Consider a linear, time-invariant system whose unit-sample response h[n] is shown in the image. Is it possible to represent this system with a finite number of poles?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The unit sample response given in the figure is h[n] = (1/2)^{n/2}, where n = 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, ...; at other n, h[n] = 0. The discrete sequence plot below also shows that only even nonnegative times have nonzero samples: at n=0 it is 1, at n=2 it is 1/2, at n=4 it is 1/4, at n=6 it is 1/8, decaying successively; odd times and negative times are 0. Reasoning: Renumber according to the even samples, let n = 2k, k >= 0, then h[2k] = (1/2)^k, and other samples are 0. Therefore the system function is H(z) = sum_{k=0}^{∞} (1/2)^k z^{-2k}. This is a geometric series, and summing gives H(z) = 1 / (1 - (1/2) z^{-2}). This H(z) is a rational function, and the denominator 1 - (1/2)z^{-2} has only finitely many roots; equivalently, the denominator can be written as z^2 - 1/2, therefore there are two poles z = ±1/sqrt(2). So this system can be represented with finitely many poles.

raw_record.question_text: Consider a linear, time-invariant system whose unit-sample response h[n] is shown in the image. Is it possible to represent this system with a finite number of poles?

method.method_draft: After reading the plotted/formula response, re-index the nonzero samples by n=2k, so h[2k]=(1/2)^k for k>=0 and h[n]=0 otherwise. Compute H(z)=sum_{k=0}^∞ (1/2)^k z^{-2k}=1/(1-(1/2)z^{-2}). Since this transfer function is rational and its denominator has only two roots, conclude the system can be represented with a finite number of poles. Answer: Yes.

推理：按照偶数样本重新编号，令 n = 2k，k >= 0，则 h[2k] = (1/2)^k，其他样本为 0。因此系统函数为 H(z) = sum_{k=0}^{∞} (1/2)^k z^{-2k}。这是一个等比级数，求和得到 H(z) = 1 / (1 - (1/2) z^{-2})。该 H(z) 是有理函数，分母 1 - (1/2)z^{-2} 只有有限个根；等价地，分母可写为 z^2 - 1/2，因此有两个极点 z = ±1/sqrt(2)。所以该系统可以用有限个极点表示。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Directly converts the visually specified even-index geometric impulse response into its Z-transform and identifies the finite set of poles; this is the natural single route for the problem.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read from the image that h[n] is nonzero only at even nonnegative indices n=0,2,4,6,... and that the samples decay as 1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, ...; equivalently h[n]=(1/2)^{n/2} for n even and 0 otherwise.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question statement to know the system is LTI and that the task is to decide whether the system can be represented with finitely many poles.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the Z-transform of a geometric sequence: sum_{k=0}^∞ a^k z^{-2k}=1/(1-a z^{-2}). A rational Z-transform has a finite number of poles, here from 1-(1/2)z^{-2}=0, giving z=±1/sqrt(2).
